utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Guy-Smith, the news in respect of your client's health is encouraging.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It seems to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I see we're at full strength. I understand there is some matter to be raised before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, I believe Mr. Nicholls would like to make an application regarding the following witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. Your Honours, I apologise for the lateness of this application, but I would like to apply for a variance in the protective measures which you have granted for the next witness who is subject of the decision which was handed down yesterday. I move that his entire testimony be heard in closed session rather than private session. I have spoken with counsel for all three accused today, this morning and just now, and there is no objection to that motion. It is based on reviewing the facts and circumstances of this person's testimony as well as with meeting the person recently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the expected duration of his evidence in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's a little bit hard for me to say, Your Honours. I haven't been in this courtroom for a while, but I think I will take, in chief, probably around three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You propose the whole of the examination, cross-examination, and re-examination be in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The great majority of his testimony, I believe, would need to be in private session anyway under the existing orders, because the substance of the testimony could identify the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not immediately clear which is the witness you intend next to call.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's number L-7, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: L-7, yes. And is there any observation any counsel for the Defence wishes to make? If --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Thank you, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Nor I. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be ordered accordingly, then, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. And if the present witness could be called in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kickert.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Two things: The apologies of the Chamber for the interruption to your evidence yesterday because of a health problem of an accused; and if I could remind you of the affirmation at the beginning of your evidence which is still applicable. Yes, Mr. Whiting [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Black: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, when we finished yesterday we were finishing with your first meeting with the KLA, sometime in late July, I think you said, 1998. When was the next time that you met with members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was just the very next day, when I again went to Malisevo and this time on my own without the Secretary-General who left Kosovo already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom did you meet at this second meeting?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see Number 7 again, but I also met with what was called a Number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know now who number 3 is?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Hashim Thaqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the first time you had met Hashim Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what his position within the KLA was at that time?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know. But after having met Number 7, I assumed that Number 3 would be higher in the hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, did you prepare a report of this meeting after it was over?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you should have a bundle of documents that was given to you yesterday. If you could look at the first of those documents bearing the number U008-1196 at the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be -- do you find that document, Mr. Kickert? To be clear, that's the German version, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the date of that document?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's 24th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you identify it for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document I have written. It's -- it states on top -- it says: "SB" which means "Herr General Secretaire," so I am the author of this report and it states my name next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be given the next Prosecution Exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P56.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And with Mr. Younis's assistance, I would like to put the English version of this document on the Sanction system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, do you see that on your computer screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps if the usher could assist him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I see a document, but I can't read it. Can you focus it a little more?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Younis has now zoomed in on a part of your document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it legible on your screen, Mr. Kickert?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hardly, but I can read it. The italics are a little difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry to get into the technicalities. In front of you, you have several buttons. One says computer evidence.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now it's legible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Kickert, if you would look at heading 1 of that document which says "Government of nationality or round table." And please read the highlighted section which has now been blown up on your screen.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The embassy reports that it met with high-ranking representatives of the KLA, number 3 and 7, who are also ideologists of the KLA," which is, may I allow, not a perfect translation of what I have written in German, because I -- "who are considered to be the ideologists of the KLA," is what I have written in German, "in a very open and constructive debate on 23 July in Malisevo."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that and thank you for the correction. I would invite you any time you notice a discrepancy in the translation, please do mention it.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you continue with that part highlighted there.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In italics it was a remark of mine, where I stated that probably "no. 1 either does not exist at all or has a seat abroad; no. 7 who was met by head of office" -- this is a wrong translation again, with the secretary-general, somebody. "HGS" in German would be the Herr General Secretaire -- said that he was aware of the position of the secretary-general "at the time but excused his conduct by stating that they were primarily soldiers in the KLA and had no experience dealing with the diplomats. It continues, "Gani Krasniqi was a KLA commander and took part in setting up the KLA in Malisevo," so this is what I thought at the time. And then it continues: "'Spokesperson' Jakup Krasniqi is only no. 11 or 12 in the hierarchy." This is also an assumption of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my next question. Where does this information come from, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have come from talks I had [inaudible] in Pristina, speculations more than any proof. I had no direct information which number Jakup Krasniqi was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd ask you and -- with Mr. Younis's help to look a little further in the document under heading 2, KLA. It's on your screen now, and if Mr. Younis could blow up the highlighted section. Mr. Kickert, would you read that to me and I promise I won't just ask you to read all day today.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The dissension within the KLA, which has been obvious to observers in recent days, was found to have dissipated for the most part in Malisevo." Yeah, that's a more or less correct translation. "It was supposed that the Decani KLA wanted to ensure the support of the U.S.A. for the KLA by coming closer to the LDK (according to the KLA's headquarters a commander of the 1st KLA brigade never welcomed the constitution" -- I think this is a wrong translation. This is a very wrong translation, sorry to say that. If I may try to translate. It was supposed that the UCK of Decani wanted, through a line which was near to the LDK, which is a political party of the then Gllogovc, tried to get the support of the USA for the UCK. And then in brackets it says that -- meaning that the UCK Decani had welcomed the constitution -- not the constitution, or the getting together the parliament, and this was done by a commander of the 1st UCK Brigade. And in my talks they refuted that. A 1st UCK Brigade didn't exist at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could continue reading, and I apologise you're having to correct the translation a little bit, but I think this last sentence on this English translation which continues to the next page, if you could read that, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This is interpreted by the KLA headquarters as an attempt to create division by the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will move on to the next page, Mr. Younis.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "By the LDK. An article by Enver Maloku, leader of the Kosovo Information Centre of the LDK, in which he accused the KLA of irresponsible behaviour in Orahovac which took the lives of hundreds of civilians, also contributed to the increasingly fractured relationship between the KLA and the LDK. (Maloku was recently the victim of the mysterious assassination attempt.)" If I may look at the German translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, I think you have briefly alluded to this, but could you explain to the Trial Chamber what the LDK was, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The LDK is a political party -- it was and it still is headed by Ibrahim Rugova. It is the Democratic League of Kosovo and it was the main political party in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would direct your attention to the second-to-last line. Mr. Younis, if you could just put that back. If I could direct your attention to the phrase: "increasingly fractured relationship between the KLA and the LDK." Could you please explain that reference.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is two things I would add to that. At that time there was talk of an armed group called FARK, which is the armed forces of the Republic of Kosova, which was a group supposedly supported by the LDK, more concretely by Mr. Bujar Bukoshi who was the prime minister in exile at that time. And the second issue is that those who took up arms were dissatisfied with the policy of the LDK, which they found as too passive. So those who criticised the LDK and Dr. Rugova were in my assessment two groups: those who wanted to have a more activist policy but still stay in an unarmed -- by an unarmed means, mainly students with the demonstration but also some political parties in Pristina; then they had the KLA which took up the arms struggle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand that these different positions caused certain tension between the KLA and the LDK?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's an assessment I did take and I stick to that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One other thing I would note before moving on. There are several references in these paragraphs that you've read to "KLA headquarters." Is that a reference to Malisevo that you described earlier?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We believe that the headquarters were in Malisevo at that time, but we had nothing to corroborate it. But it's -- it was our feeling at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: With Mr. Younis's assistance I would like to direct your attention to the last highlighted section of this page. If it can be blown up, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, would you also read this.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With regard to the disputes within the KLA it now appears that the breakaway KLA factions of the central command in Malisevo where the commanders of the Drenica region (Likovc) are directly represented, have again been brought into line." If I may take a look at the German version just to check. Maybe more correct would be: The KLA factions which -- and then I have it [French spoken] from the central command, who did not follow the central command in Malisevo. This is a reference where I thought the central command was, as they claimed, were brought into line. It continues: "A simple soldier risen to stardom, Lum Haxhiu, who placed himself in the right-hand side of the photo during Holbrooke's visit to Junik and afterwards had people talk about him was, according to the headquarters in Malisevo, instructed not to make any further comments which he is now respecting." If I may give some background. Lum Haxhiu was a KLA soldier who, when Richard Holbrooke, the US envoy visited Junik in western Kosovo, had pictures taken and cameras, some film footage taken with Richard Holbrooke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, then. This reference to "breakaway KLA factions," as it appears in this translation, was that just this particular incident or did you know that to be a problem for the KLA more generally?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that -- I think we should be careful. Lum Haxhiu was not somebody who broke away from the KLA. He was talking to the press and I think that was not welcomed. There was a general problem I understood or I assessed at the time that in western Kosovo there were some armed groups who would not -- who would do their own things and not necessarily follow any other command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was Fatmir Limaj ever in that position of being at odds with the KLA leadership?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I think we're finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do have one more question regarding this meeting. It's not in the report, but do you remember if you raised the Geneva Conventions with Hashim Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Because the same day I was in Malisevo, the ICRC representatives were also looking for interlocutor because they wanted to flag the issue of respect of Geneva Convention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if Mr. Thaqi made any statements regarding that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did assure they would respect the Geneva Conventions, because they are regular army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kickert. We'll leave that meeting now. And if I could ask you, when was your next meeting with members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was later on, still in July 1998 when after Malisevo was abandoned by the KLA. So I -- we got lost -- we were at loss who to speak to within the KLA. So my next, if you like, target or interlocutor I was looking for was somebody who appeared in July as the spokesperson of the KLA. That was Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you arrange to meet with Mr. Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was through local journalists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Klecka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the route you took to travel to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a little bit of a detour. We went through this nature reserve park, where also hunting took place. We went through that. And then very south of the Londenica valley [phoen] we crossed into the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I would like to hand the witness a map that we used yesterday. It's map 6 in the maps booklet, Prosecution Exhibit 1, Your Honours. If we could please see the ELMO on our computer screens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, in the meantime, if you could see if you could find the pointer that we used yesterday as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And could we zoom out from the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry. Perhaps before we move to the next document, I wonder if the Prosecution are seeking to exhibit the translation of the German document which has been put in. Obviously it's been referred to by the witness in English as well, but currently there is no exhibit number assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Absolutely. Your Honour, my preference would be to exhibit the English and the German versions together under one number or it can be .1, however you would prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I had assumed that is what you were doing. But I think you can take it that both language versions will be the one exhibit number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And I was going to ask the audio/visual booth to zoom out from the map if we could, please. That should be sufficient. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, please point out to the Trial Chamber the route that you took to this meeting in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to describe the route with 100 per cent certainty. So -- I just know what we went through what is called Lipovac. It was the nature reserve I was mentioning earlier. And how we got there from Pristina, I don't know. But we went through this and crossed here, this valley in the south to get up to Klecka here. So this is the route I'm sure about, that -- Lipovac up here and to here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Kickert, once you were in Klecka, where was this meeting held, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a house. I can't recall how it looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the room that the meeting was held in?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I remember is that I had a deja vu entering the room, that there was a computer, an image I had seen on a local -- a photograph, or local media before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could see Sanction on our computer screens once again, I would like to show the witness a clip from Prosecution Exhibit P34. For the record, this clip begins about 16 minutes, 51 seconds into this. Mr. Younis, could you play this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If you could pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, do you recognise the room in this video?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise this image, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the place where your meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify any of the men in this photo or in this video?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise two persons: Jakup Krasniqi sitting, and to his right is Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit, Mr. Younis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I just interrupt there. Mr. Kickert, when you said "to his right," did you mean that literally, that is, the right hand of the person sitting in the middle? Or did you mean to the right as we view it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the right as we view it or at the left from the sitting person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification, Your Honour. Now I believe we're done with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, who attended this meeting from your side?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was accompanied by David Slinn, my colleague from the British embassy in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the KLA there was Jakup Krasniqi, who we wanted to go see, and there was also Rame Buja and also Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was Fatmir Limaj introduced to you at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was introduced as Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the first time you had met Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually come to know him fairly well?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn Commander Celiku's real name?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much later, probably 1999 sometime. Either -- I'm not sure, but maybe at the Rame Buja or just after the bombing campaign.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're on this -- if I could also show on Sanction --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a photograph bearing the ERN U003-3244. It was included in Prosecution Exhibit P24. So we have seen this before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, do you recognise anyone in this photo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please name them for us.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the left from how we view it is Rexhep Selimi; in the middle is Hashim Thaqi; and to the right is Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this how Fatmir Limaj appeared when you met him in July 1998, as near as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I did see him in 1998/1999 once with beard, once without beard. So I don't know if at that meeting he had a beard or not. But most probably he had, and I saw him afterwards without a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We're finished with that photograph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the content of this third meeting. Mr. Kickert, had you prepared an agenda in anticipation of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did -- or I did it together with David Slinn, my British colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document on Sanction. It bears the ERN U008-1333. By the way, Mr. Kickert, you also have these documents in that bundle, so if you do have trouble seeing what's on the screen, feel free to refer to the hard copy. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the agenda for the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honours, I would ask that it receive the next Prosecution exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P57.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. If Mr. Younis could assist us once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask that you look at the first highlighted section there. It may be a little hard to read, but could you read that for us, Mr. Kickert.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Cease-fire is not a defeat (war crimes on all sides are not amnestied). Act responsible. Window of opportunity."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the third highlighted section on that page, if you could read that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Prisoners of war, Geneva Convention - no civilians access to the ICRC."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain what you intended to raise here.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The idea was that we would remind a spokesperson of the KLA, Jakup Krasniqi, that the KLA should respect the Geneva Conventions and that no civilians should be taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if anything in particular prompted you to raise this issue?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just a general concern. There was a lot of media talk about abduction and detentions, but we had not had any confirmation on that whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the issue was in fact discussed at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would point your attention, then, to the second highlighted section, which is at the middle of 3, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We can close those others. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read that for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The IC," international community, "may well accomplish idea of sending troops to northern Albania."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a contemplation of sending NATO troops to northern Albania to stabilise the region. And this we may have raised for, if you like, the carrot-and-stick approach; as a possible stick saying if NATO troops are in northern Albania, then it would not be as easy as it may have been before to have bases in northern Albania for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have information that the KLA had such bases in northern Albania?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no real information on that, but it was the assumption. But I had no proof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We've finished with that document. I'd like to show you the next document which bears the ERN U008-1332.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And I just mention, Your Honours, both the last document and this document are attached to his statement as well if that's an easier place to find them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the notes of your meeting with Mr. Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At this point I would ask that they be given a Prosecution Exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P58.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If I could ask Mr. Younis to zoom in on the first two highlighted sections together, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, that's difficult to read. Perhaps on the hard copy could you indicate what those say.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the top one says: "Celiku," and the left one says "COMM."and then the wrong writing, so "Sheliku," S-h.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Comm, what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a reference to Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could move on to the next section, please. Please read just the first, the small highlighted two words, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "VJ mainly."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain this note, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: VJ is the Yugoslav army, and that was that -- I suppose, but -- I read the report, but that means their concern was mainly on the VJ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think the KLA was mainly concerned with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe they were -- had better equipment, tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Better than whom?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Than the police, the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could move to the next highlighted section -- well, it's still there, it's already blown up. If you could read that, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Army to retreat, all people to return, checkpoint away." And then these were the -- then: "3 conditions for not attacking."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this correspond generally to cease-fire that you had mentioned in your agenda?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of our aims was that we were pleading to them to refrain from any attacks, because at that time, just to give the background, we were attempting to form a joint Kosovar platform to be able to negotiate with Belgrade. So our aim was that through their military restraint it would be made easier for us to come to this joint platform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I direct your attention to the next highlighted section. What does that say?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Serbs not accept No longer front war (people removed)."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does this mean?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this as I have written in my report, it says that if these conditions are not accepted we will change the tactics from a front war to guerrilla war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mention your report. Perhaps we'll return to this with the next exhibit. Before we move on, the last highlighted section. Could you read that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Very wrong if people think the roads are free."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was meant by this?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a long period in May and even June of 1998, some of the main roads through Kosovo were blocked by the KLA. And probably at that time they had the Serb security forces may have re-established control of the main roads. And this is just reference that they could at any time attack these roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe we're finished with that document. And I'll take you to a third and final document with regard to this same meeting. If I could show you ERN U008-1193, which you should have in hard copy as well if that's easier. Do you recognise this document, Mr. Kickert?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I recognise the German one, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you identify it, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have written this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At this point I would ask that it be given a Prosecution exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P59, that's the German version. The English translation will be P59A, and the Albanian translation, Prosecution Exhibit P59B.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have the English version on the Sanction screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Younis, could you zoom in on the first highlighted section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, please read that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "After the EU troika was unable to establish contact with the high-ranking KLA representatives regarding the consequences of the most recent combat activities" -- that is a wrong translation: Due to the consequences of the most recent combat activities -- "on 30 July the desk officer and a British colleague drove (for approximately two hours in an armoured British Land Rover in part on side roads built by the KLA itself) to the new KLA 'headquarters' that was moved to the area of north of Crnoljevo, where they met with KLA spokesman Jakup Krasniqi, the regional commander Celiku, and Rame Buja, former LDK secretary and now a KLA staff member." General Staff member would probably be a more correct translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You read "the new KLA headquarters moved to Crnoljevo. Is that a reference to Klecka that you referred to before?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I deliberately left out the name of the exact location, because even if that report was confidential, you never know if somebody drops a name somewhere else and I didn't want to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you omitted the name to protect the KLA headquarters, the security of that place.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I lost my interlocutors when the KLA abandoned Malisevo. I didn't want to have it happen a second time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The word headquarters, as you noted, appears in quotation marks. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was no certainty, so that is why I put it into quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What made you think that Klecka may have been a headquarters, as you say there?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I met the spokesperson, Jakup Krasniqi, there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that same paragraph, you refer to the "regional commander Celiku." Is this something you were told or is this your own impression of him?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my own impression. He was introduced me as Commander Celiku and my assumption is if he is in that meeting he might be a regional one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let's move to the next -- I believe it's the next page of the document. And if Mr. Younis would highlight both of those highlighted sections, if he would zoom in on those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, please read just the first part there.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Viewed on the whole, the overall impression remained that the KLA had not yet completed its internal opinion-forming process."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this a reference to? Could you explain.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the main aim of this meeting was to talk on, as I said, this formation of a united Kosovar political platform to enter negotiations with Belgrade. So my impression was that the internal opinion-forming process within the KLA has not yet been completed, which means they were still discussing it. They were critical of some issues. There was a list of persons presented actually the day before, if I'm not mistaken, in another place in the north, in Likovc, by the designated, if you want to call it, at that time, Prime Minister Mehemet Hajziri, who went there with the U.S. envoy Chris Hill to see the KLA in Likovc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did the opinion-forming process referred to here have any connection with military decision-making?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am a diplomat. I was never interested in military hierarchies. I just wanted to have a person who would be able politically to speak authoritative [sic] in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can move on to the last or the second-last page of this document. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Younis, please zoom in on the top highlighted section.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters require that the witness please will speak a little bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, I think I would ask you to read this paragraph for the Trial Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In an initial reaction KLA representatives completely rejected Nekiba Kelmendi of the LDK and demanded participation from the LPK," another political party, "at the desk officer's objection that the LPK is actually a party of Albanians abroad, it was claimed that a wing existed even within the Kosovo itself) the LDK representatives are causing problems for the KLAs as a matter of principle; it was made clear by Austria/UK that no common platform would be possible out LDK participation." If I may just look at the German version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, well, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. First, it may be helpful if you would explain what the LPK was.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a political party which was actually to -- what our understanding was was active abroad and a lot of the -- or many of the KLA fighters came out of the LPK, to my understanding. But not necessarily as -- those persons I also met in this meeting, Jakup Krasniqi, for example, and Rame Buja both came from the LDK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I direct your attention to the phrase: "The LDK representatives are causing problems for the KLA as a matter of principle." Could you explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, there was a friction between the KLA and the LDK. I may try to recall the context. When the KLA emerged and they are in -- openly in 1998 and then gained ground in spring of 1998, the LDK tried to exert its dominance and was calling for elections, presidential elections. So there was sort of a little bit of friction of who would dominate the political scene. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would direct your attention a bit further down the page. Yes, under heading 3, KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Younis, please zoom in on the first highlighted section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read this, Mr. Kickert.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The KLA representatives who were met with" -- "who we met with," it should read -- "confirmed the change in their tactics. It is clear for them that a conventional war with well-defined front lines is not possible and they will therefore confine themselves to guerrilla actions." "Confine themselves" is not a correct translation, but they would "move to" guerrilla actions. "The threat was reiterated that actions in big towns, such as Pristina, could always be started." Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, was this essentially what you alluded to in your notes with the words: "If the Serbs no longer accept a front war"?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand the KLA to be saying that they were going to use guerrilla tactics as a tactical decision?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm not a military expert, but that was a time when they had to retreat from certain areas like Malisevo. So the change of -- yeah, military tactics, yeah. So what they've done before in the very beginning of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last sentence you read was: "The threat was reiterated that actions in big towns, such as Pristina, could always be started." Was the KLA capable of attacking a big town like Pristina or I should say of undertaking actions in a big town such as Pristina at that time?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to judge that. There were some armed actions not too far from Pristina. But that I really can't assess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In that same paragraph, if we could highlight the next sentence. Please read that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In addition, they stated that it would be wrong to presume now that the streets are safe and passable." That's a correct translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One translation issue I would ask about. In your notes you refer to roads being safe, and I believe in the German you use the word "strassen," which here is translated as streets.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's roads. It is a main artery is what is meant by that. So it would be, rather, roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say the main arteries. Do you refer to roads between cities and towns as opposed to streets, I guess, in cities and towns?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I refer to roads in the main towns, say from Pristina to Pec/Peja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could briefly look at the last highlighted section there. You don't need to read this out, but I would ask you if these are the three requirements we saw in your notes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We're finished with that document. Mr. Kickert, did you continue to meet with the KLA after July 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These meetings were interrupted as since sort of mid-July 1998, the Serbian security forces launched an offensive. So the places where I used to meet them I could not meet them anymore. And then in 1998 -- in August of 1998 we were concentrating our activities more on the IDP crisis. Through the offensive of the Serbian security forces a lot of people left their homes. And so we in August tried to see how we could counter that. And at the same time the US had taken the position to form a negotiation team with LDK representatives only. This decision was endorsed by the contact group. So the KLA was no longer welcome in this negotiation team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, did you have occasion to meet with Commander Celiku again during 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Later on in the fall of 1998 when at that time the KVM or the Kosovo Verification Mission of the OSCE was established we did have contact with KLA representatives again. It was Hashim Thaqi mainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Fatmir Limaj ever accompany Hashim Thaqi at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at least in one of the meetings in Banja, he was with Hashim Thaqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To return briefly to one thing we discussed earlier. You said when you first met Hashim Thaqi he introduced himself as Number 3. Do you remember when you learned his real name?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually learnt his name right away, but I never used it. Only when it was -- it became public knowledge, that was in the fall of 1998, I suppose, did I use it as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come to see Hashim Thaqi more as a military or a political figure?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were just interested in political figures. I saw him as a political figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Fatmir Limaj? In the summer of 1998, did you see him as a military or political figure?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present at the meetings, but he was not my interlocutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember, did he appear at those meetings in uniform?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes; so did Hashim Thaqi also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We've been discussing 1998. Mr. Kickert, did you later work with UNMIK after 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were your duties briefly?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the political advisor to the SRSG, Bernard Kushner, from summer 1999 until the end of 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that position did you have contact with Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. Fatmir Limaj became an official of the PDK political party, which was established in 1999. And in this role we met actually more often than we ever did in 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a good relationship with Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your impression of him in 1999 and 2000?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I regarded him and I still regard him very highly. I think he's a person -- in my dealings with him, I could -- I sensed that he had -- is a man of responsibility and of pragmatism and somebody who was not an ideologist or somebody who -- with radical ideas. He was open for reconciliation. Since we didn't have a common language, we spoke Serbo-Croatian with each other. So a very open person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time did you ever hear allegations that troops under Limaj's command were abducting civilians?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever heard of a KLA prison in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to visit Fatmir Limaj in his home?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did visit him in 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please briefly describe that visit.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was one of my trips on weekends. As you tend to stay in Pristina too much and you won't grasp Kosovo if you don't go outside the capital, I did my weekend outings. In one of the outings I went to Banja where without any planning we just asked whether Mr. Limaj was in his own village. We did meet him and he received us in his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that visit tell you anything about the status which Fatmir Limaj enjoyed in that area?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. When we met him, there were -- we were not alone. There was some other persons with him, also elder people. And we were sitting the traditional way on the floor and drinking tea and -- I don't smoke, but smoking. Yeah, I could sense that he commanded a lot of respect in his community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am about to change topic somewhat. We're done with Mr. Kickert's meetings with KLA members and I think it may be an appropriate time to take the break, as you please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] we'd normally be sitting for another 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm perfectly happy to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm still getting used to the times of the breaks. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, I'm now going to go through a few documents with you, I think five, from the months of June and July which I hope may assist the Trial Chamber to understand the situation in Kosovo at the time. The first one I would show you is an 8 June 1998, report from the Belgrade embassy to the Austrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. If Mr. Younis could put this up. The German version bears the number U008-1208 to 1209. The English translation is U003-7981 to 83. Have you found that report -- excuse me, have you found that document? Mr. Kickert, did you write this report?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I would ask that it be assigned an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P60, the German version; the English translation P60A; and the Albanian translation P60B.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By way of introduction, I suppose, Mr. Kickert, I would ask you to read the highlighted summary and if Mr. Younis could zoom in on that for us, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: First sentence reads: "Serbian security forces appear to have no control over road links Pristina-Pec and Kosovska Mitrovica-Pec."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just read each point. Just the bullet points, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just check with the German version first. Second one: "Stretch of road between Djakovica and Pec still closed to private traffic. "Fighting along the Pec-Djakovica road has ceased; now evidently concentrated around the Decani and surroundings." This is a wrong translation. It should read that the fightings which have ceased on the road between Pec and Djakovica were evidently concentrated on Decani and its surroundings. So not now evidently concentrated. They had ceased. The fighting has ceased when we visited. Fourth bullet point: "UCK seems to have interrupted road links for a certain period." This is a correct translation and it refers to the third bullet point, the Pec-Djakovica stretch of road. And the next bullet point: "Considerable devastation in Decani, but less than alleged by LDK and less than in Drenica in March," and I put Lausa, but it could have been also other places as well. "Conspicuous fire damage (arson). "Situation in Decani tense; majority of inhabitants appear to have left. "Areas bordering on Albania were not shown. "Fresh assurances by Yug. For. Min. that battle region is now open to diplomats."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would now direct your attention to the highlighted section at the bottom of the document. I won't ask you to read that -- actually -- well, perhaps the second part. Beginning: "It was noticeable," please read that.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It was noticeable that the direct road connection between Pristina and Pec, and between Kosovska Mitrovica and Pec, through the Drenica region, were avoided."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I can ask Mr. Younis if we can continue on to the next page, just to complete that thought.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The reason given in response to inquiries was that safety could not be guaranteed on this stretch of road."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Kickert, in other words, you were told in 1998 that the Pristina-Pec road was blocked or unsafe. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it was unsafe for us to travel, us diplomats. Just to give the context, this was a trip organised by the Yugoslav foreign ministry for diplomats based in Belgrade to show them the region which is called in Albanian, Dugadjin Gorani, in western Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It might be helpful with the assistance of Mr. Younis and the usher if I could show you a map. It's -- I would ask for map 4 from the maps booklet to be given to the witness and placed on the ELMO. Mr. Kickert, again with your pointer if you could indicate the route that you took to the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were flown into Pristina and then instead of taking the direct road from Pristina to Pec/Peja, we were taken northwards through Mitrovica and then all the way to Rozaj [phoen] in Montenegro down to Pec/Peja. And we continued south to Decani and to a village which was called Prileb [phoen], or so-called Prileb. And we continued this whole trip in southwards to Prizren and this road back to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you just pause there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes seem to be having subsisting problems with LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, whilst there's a pause in proceedings, I needn't be recorded. My client states that the translation into Albanian appears rather rushed, so perhaps if we slow down it will make the translators' jobs somewhat easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you for the reminder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we may be operational now. Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Should I go back and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told that it is all being recorded so that it will be included in a short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. If we could move then back to the document that we were viewing before. I don't have it on my screen. I think it's -- okay. Thanks. I've got it now. And if Mr. Younis could -- yes, if you could zoom in on that entire paragraph, please, go down -- yeah, that's great.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, could you please read the first highlighted section there.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Decani: Considerable devastation, but by no means as drastic as described by LDK (80 per cent destroyed; a second Vukovar)".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe what you saw in Decani.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I may give the background. Our information on what was going on in Kosovo at that time was very scarce. So informations that we got or either official Serb information or what we got from the LDK. And I refer to this description of LDK, is allowing descriptions of LDK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a reference to Vukovar. Had you yourself in fact been at Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain it to the Trial Chamber. I'm not sure if they are aware of the reference, although they probably are.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Vukovar was a city in eastern -- or still a city in eastern Croatia which was heavily shelled by Serb forces and the devastation there could still be seen when I was in Vukovar in 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the reference here is to say that the destruction was not as serious as that in Vukovar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The destruction was not at the same level. Not to say that there was no destruction, but it was at the same level. My assessment what we had heard from the LDK was an exaggeration. And we have to know that both sides in this tried to give their own spin, knowing that the western diplomats didn't have information, what was going on on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But just to be clear there did appear to be evidence of fighting at Decani?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. No doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last phrase I suppose of that paragraph which is highlighted. Could you read that, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states: "Colleagues who visited the Drenica region in March reported comparatively little destruction (no shelling with heavy within weaponry)".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this indicate that the destruction in Drenica in March then was more than what you saw in Decani? Am I reading that correctly?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I referred to colleagues and they were most probably military attaches which were also on this trip. And they had seen the Drenica region where the March events happened. I didn't, at that time. And they made a comparison and their comparison was that in Drenica they were shelling, where there was no shelling from tanks in the Dugadjin Gorani area at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can close that box and if it's possible to highlight that entire last box. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, this refers to a briefing by the Yugoslav foreign ministry and minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Police activity a response to murders and abductions of policemen, but especially to an attempt by 'terrorist gangs' to block the main road."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the reference to police activity, does that refer to the Serb forces who were responsible for the destruction that you had seen?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the police activity, that refers to what was going on in the Dugadjin area in this stretch we saw between Pec/Peja, Betonaj [phoen], and then to Prila [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know you're not a military expert, but I wonder if you could indicate to the Court: When they talk about police activity this is not regular patrol of the streets or regular police activities we're used to. It's something more; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise. Maybe I misheard. Was the objection that I was leading him or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can repeat myself. I simply stated the obvious, with respect, that the witness can answer for himself. He can describe, no doubt, what was the police activity that he was alluding to. I don't think Mr. Black needs to press him in a certain direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have we addressed that adequately?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I'll move on to the next part of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the next bullet point, Mr. Kickert, I have highlighted: "Border is secured by the army." Do you if the VJ was concentrated on the borders?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is where -- the army was there for border security, but I didn't see any army, no VJ when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I suppose what I was trying to ask very inartfully before: Can you briefly indicate to us the difference between army activity and what is called police activity in your report.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this section, I cite out of the briefing of the Yugoslav foreign ministry, so they refer to police activity. And this is not an assessment of mine, but just mirroring what we were briefed on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I don't think there's any reason to belabour the point. The last phrase of that bullet point makes a reference to ensuring safety on the roads. What roads does that refer to? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was this stretch which -- between Pec/Peja and Decani, I suppose. Because this was a road which was accessible again. That's why they took us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read the next two bullet points.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Dramatic increase in 'terrorist attacks' since beginning of year (409 by 3 June, with 53 fatalities including 18 police)."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next bullet point.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Albanians accused of carrying out ethnic cleansing."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, these are figures and allegations of the Serb authorities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am just giving there what we were told in the briefing. It's just that my ministry knows what we were told there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the Serbs alleging that the Albanians were attacking civilians?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if they refer to ethnic cleansing, I suppose so. But it's not me to interpret them [sic].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read the next bullet point.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "UCK attempting to connect Drenica and Malisevo areas with western Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the KLA control the Drenica and Malisevo areas at this time?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what we thought at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would be the advantage of attempting to connect those areas with western Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, two areas of fighting and the western Kosovo was adjacent to northern Albania, which was considered as a -- for logistical reasons for smuggling in weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could turn briefly to the next page and I'll wrap this up with this document -- well, wrap up this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read just that last bullet point please, Mr. Kickert.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is again from the briefing of the Yugoslav Serb side. "Training camps and ordnance depots for UCK in Albania (at least three)".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Next bullet point.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presentation of weaponry: Arms, including 2 bazookas and a small Howitzer belonging to the JVA." And then comes my assessment: "Looked old, partly rusted or unused (but SB lacks expertise in this sphere)".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may be obvious, can you explain for the record what a bazooka is.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something you put on your shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a Howitzer?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you lacked of experience in this sphere, Mr. Kickert. Have you ever served in the military?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We're finished with that document, Your Honour, it may be an appropriate time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be and we will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, I've been reminded that I need to pause after your answers before my question. And I would ask that you also pause for a second, if you could remember, after my questions before answering. And perhaps also on those occasions where I ask you to read, if you could just be conscious to read a little bit more slowly. Thank you. Mr. Kickert, I would like to show you another document. It bears the ERN 0081-1205. It's a 27 June 1998 document. If you could locate that, please. Mr. Kickert, did you write in report?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I wrote this report together with my ambassador.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The English version is there on our computer screens. I would ask Mr. Younis to zoom in on the first bullet point, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, would you please read just the highlighted text.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "UCK blockade of the mainly Serbian town of Kijevo soon to be ended (the US believes that the FRY army could breach the blockade at any time but is holding back for political reasons)."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We may return to this topic with another document, but just one question before we move on. Was the KLA capable of blockading entire towns like Kijevo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I understood at that time, the main road where Kijevo was located on, meaning the road between Pristina and Pec/Peja, was blocked. And therefore the town or the village of Kijevo had or no secure access to these main towns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did that situation exist, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been for a couple of weeks. A US envoy even called Kijevo the most dangerous place on earth at a certain stage, referring to the possibility of escalation due to what was perceived as a blockade of this town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could highlight the next bullet point, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, please read that.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Visible increase in militarisation and professionalisation of the UCK, according to the US military attache." If I may, I think it's incorrect if you use the word "militarisation." It sounds more like an ideological thing. What was meant is they had more military armament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we zoom in on the final highlighted bullet point, please. Mr. Kickert, please read that bullet point.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The UCK command structure nevertheless remains something of a mystery, according to the US. Although the UCK operates with terms such as 'General Staff,' in the US view it is more a matter of diffuse horizontal command and coordination structures. This could be problematical in terms of involving the UCK in the political dialogue."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before it slips my attention again, could I have this document marked as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P62, the German version; the English translation will be P61A; and the Albanian translation P61B.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, there's a reference that "the UCK command structure remains something of a mystery according to the US." Do you know what the basis was for that assessment?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assessment was probably also to find interlocutors, and that they were as much as we were puzzled as who would be it. And since you had no idea of the structure of this organisation, it was difficult to identify somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The term "General Staff" appears in quotation marks. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was used, but we were not sure or not aware of its existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard of a KLA general staff by June of 1998, the time of this document?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I use this term, it must have been in use, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned a KLA central command in some of the documents we viewed earlier today. Is that a reference to the same thing as "general staff," or is that something different?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would be the same. Again, I'm not a military person. And if I use these terms I either have heard them or I wouldn't be using them maybe in the correct military sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, again in your understanding, taking into consideration the fact that you're not a military expert, did you understand that central command or general staff to be regional in scope or to cover all of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my assessment -- I think during 1998 and I don't know when, there was certainly an effort that it would be all of Kosovo. But my feeling was that the coordination between different regions was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about coordination within regions?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell. I was involved in the political scene. And whenever we brought them a proposal to consider, it took them a considerable time -- actually, a very long time to come up with a decision and I think throughout my dealings with the KLA I had the feeling that there was a larger group involved in decision-making and the decisions were taken more on a consensus, less on a hierarchical basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we'll move on to another document. I'd like to show you a 1 July 1998 report from the embassy to the ministry of foreign affairs. It bears the ERN I believe 0081-1203 to 1204. Mr. Kickert, did you write this report as well?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would be asked that it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. If Mr. Younis would highlight the first section there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, please read this text to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "According to," and this in translation into English would be local press reports, "Kosovo's prefect, Veljko Odalovic, confirmed to the Reuters on the 30th of June that the Yugoslav army (VJ) participated in operations in relation to Balacevac. This would be the first time that participation of the VJ in inland operations had been confirmed by the Serbian side."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would ask you to read the other highlighted section of that document.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Odalovic is also believed to have stated to Reuters that (police) action is also scheduled to take place at the end of this week in order to liberate the strategically important place of Kijevo (along the Pec-Pristina road, which connects the UCK-controlled areas of Drenica and Malisevo). For weeks, the UCK has surrounded this place, as well as 200 Serbian civilians and dozens of police officers."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We touched briefly on Kijevo before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At this point, if -- I would like maybe with the usher's assistance to have map 6 from Prosecution Exhibit P1 back on the ELMO. Perhaps if we could zoom out a little bit more, if possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, can you point to Kijevo on this map, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Is it possible to zoom the map out any further -- no, I guess we can't. There now, we've moved it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you pointing to Kijevo now.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm pointing to Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, the document uses the words "strategically important place of Kijevo along the Pec-Pristina road." Could you explain why this area was strategically important.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: One, it was on the main road between Pristina and Pec/Peja. And this is also a junction where the road leads to the south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe earlier you mentioned that this road could somehow assist in access to northern Albanian. Would control of this area or this road by the KLA have any impact on Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
