utterances.text: No. I think I have to correct you. The road which I was mentioning which was important to have access to northern Albanian if you controlled it, it was the one south -- going south from Pec/Peja to Decani, and not this east/west between Pristina and Pec/Peja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. Was the Pec-Pristina road also strategically important?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. It went through the middle of Kosovo and it connected two big towns: the capital, Pristina, and Pec/Peja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could direct your attention back to the document and ask Mr. Younis to turn the page for us on Sanction. If you could read that first highlighted sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pavle Bulatovic, Yugoslav Minister of Defence, stated on the 30th of June that up to 55 persons had been kidnapped, including 50 Serbs and Montenegrins."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard other information about kidnappings of civilians?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I'm just citing an official from Belgrade. There had been, time and again in Serb media, allegations of kidnappings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could please look at the last highlighted section. If you would read that for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Serbia claims that they control all the cities and a large number of connecting roads in Kosovo, despite the areas controlled by the UCK (estimated at approximately 30-40 per cent Demaqi: 50 per cent) is true in relation to the cities, but completely false in relation to the roads." May I take a look at the German version?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's fine. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take your time if you want to have a look at it. There's no rush. I believe it's the last paragraph of that document, if that should help.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. It would be probably the bulk of the connecting roads. Yeah. But that is a mix of what they claim, and then my assessment saying, well, they don't have control of the roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the estimations of area controlled by the KLA, 30-40 per cent or Demaqi 50 per cent?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is just speculation. You could never -- never really tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they numbers that you came up with yourself or had you heard them, had you been told these numbers?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just heard them and being told. That's why directly I -- Mr. Demaqi who is a politician who claimed that 50 per cent were under control of the UCK. And other estimates were 30 to 40 per cent, it would have been media, it would have been maybe some military attaches. Or at that time -- at that time we had already our observers on the ground, so it may have been their estimates because they were travelling through Kosovo outside of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll proceed to the next document. It should bear the ERN 0081-1201 to 1202, and it's a 6th July 1998 report from the embassy in Belgrade to the ministry in Vienna. Mr. Kickert, did you write this report?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And it is largely in English because from the beginning, 1st of July, Austria had taken up the presidency of the EU. So I wrote it in English to it could be communicated to all other EU member states.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At this time I would ask that it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P63.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, could you please read the highlighted section of this document.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The route taken led from Pristina north to Kosovska Mitrovica, eastwards to G. Klina and Srbica (Albanian: Skenderaj) up to Donji Prekaz where the Jashari family compound - target of Serbian security forces actions in early March - was visited. The same route was taken in returning to Pristina. "The convoy did not enter UCK controlled areas."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I don't know if the witness still has map 4, if that would be helpful with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, if you would, please indicate that route on the map.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Pristina, north, to Mitrovica, and then south to Skenderaj. And there, just very near Skenderaj is Prekaz, where the compound of the Jashari family is situated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You write that the "convoy did not enter UCK controlled areas." If you had any UCK controlled areas in mind, could you point to them on the map.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was south of Skenderaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can move to the next document now, please, and we're done with the ELMO for the time being. Mr. Kickert, this is a 7 July 1998 report from the embassy to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. I believe it bears the ERN 0081-1198 to 1200 on the German version. Did you write this report?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it could be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P64.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We have the English version on the Sanction. Mr. Younis, could you please highlight that first section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Kickert, please read that highlighted two sentences.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In relation to the UCK: Holbrooke himself says that it is not known whether the UCK has an internal chain of command. He doubts that there is."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Mr. Holbrooke was basing his opinion on?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn then to the next page under part 3 which is headed "Demaqi talks." Could you please read that highlighted section as the last paragraph on the page.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In relation to the organisation of the UCK: "Clear organisational structures and a hierarchy were present, and he had met persons who identified themselves by using numbers (No.1, No.2, etc). "Spokesperson Jakup Krasniqi was an official UCK spokesperson, not only for the Drenica region, but for the whole of the UCK. "Although the uniformed people who Holbrooke had met were UCK members (one of them was a poet with family in Scandinavia) they had no particular ranks or positions. Those portraying themselves as UCK spokespersons abroad were not official ones." This is -- I was just citing what Mr. Demaqi told me, or the ambassador as well, told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Adem Demaqi?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a politician who had served I don't know how many decades of jail sentences in Serbian jails. And at that time he was the head of a party called Parliamentary Party of Kosovo, PPK, one of the parties in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. opposition to the leading LDK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Adem Demaqi connected to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I do not know. Later on in 1998 when we were lacking contact to KLA, he was designated the UCK spokesperson or the UCK representative in Pristina. But apparently he did have some sort of contacts, because he refers to a certain hierarchy with numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These four bullet points apparently coming from Adem Demaqi, are they consistent with the opinion of Mr. Holbrooke that we saw on the prior page?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But they helped me as he named Mr. Jakup Krasniqi as an official UCK spokesperson. That meant that I was looking after -- I couldn't see anybody in Malisevo anymore. I was looking to see Mr. Krasniqi in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Demaqi said he had met persons who identified themselves by using numbers. Was that something you were later able to confirm in your own meetings?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've mentioned, in my meetings in Malisevo they identified themselves with numbers, 3 and 7 at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He says that Jakup Krasniqi was an official UCK spokesperson, not only for the Drenica region, but for the whole of the UCK. Was this confirmed by your subsequent experience?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, he was speaking in the name of the UCK and I could not judge whether the UCK was covering the whole of Kosovo. He was a UCK spokesperson as such, not challenged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next two bullet points refer to people that Holbrooke had met. It says: "They had no particular ranks or positions." And then the next, I'm not sure if it's also related to Mr. Holbrooke, but it says: "Those persons portraying themselves as UCK spokespersons abroad were not official ones." Did this also turn out to be correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say so, because at that time the US had contact with UCK spokespersons in Geneva, Switzerland. And they have proven to be connected to the UCK afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the people who had met with Holbrooke at that time? Do you know what that is a reference to?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What we had mentioned before, Mr. Holbrooke, it must have been about mid-June, approximately, of 1998, went to Munich and he was photographed with this one KLA member in uniform with a Kalashnikov. And this refers to this meeting Holbrooke had, which was not planned as the US had told us, but going there it just happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kickert. At this time, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have your indulgence for a second and check that I have exhibit numbers for all the documents I intended to exhibit. Thank you. That seems to be the case. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kahn, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it pleases Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Kahn:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, my name is Karim Khan and I appear with lead counsel Mr. Mansfield and we represent Mr. Limaj. Hopefully we won't take up too much of your time, but your evidence is very important so please bear with us. We haven't spoken before, have we?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think I've had the pleasure of meeting you either. Is that right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that the Prosecution say that Mr. Limaj is guilty of very serious offenses.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard about the allegations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you pay ware that Mr. Limaj denies all those offenses?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of them or that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've been involved with Kosovo for quite a number of years. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting off in 1997.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In early 1998 -- I was covering since 1997, but the first time I went to Kosovo was in 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But even in 1997, when you were based in Belgrade, the focus of your responsibilities was Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political field, yes, but I also had responsibilities in the field of media and culture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that no doubt was because as you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kahn, we'll have to slow down the pace a bit for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Kickert, that was no doubt because, as you said yesterday, the Austrian government, like many others, were concerned with escalation of the crisis in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and all the efforts of the international community in general but also of the Austrian foreign ministry and later the EU was trying to be able to contain this escalation which -- how we perceived it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of course you were aware that for many, many years the Kosovar Albanian people had been subjugated, in effect, by the Serbian regime in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm very well aware of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you and your government were aware that people were reaching the point of no return, and as you said yesterday, were growing increasingly impatient with their continued aggression at the hands of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We assessed that they became very impatient, especially the young people; that's why we had student demonstrations. And after the armed conflict escalated, I am sure, because of this also, many young people joined the ranks of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course to conduct your -- or to properly involve yourself, you and your colleagues in the international diplomatic corps were trying to find somebody to talk to in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. We needed some interlocutors who could speak authentically and authoritatively in the name of the KLA, so that we had somebody to involve in the political process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that wasn't easy, was it?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said yesterday, it wasn't clear to you, was it, what the KLA structure was?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, for the longest time it wasn't clear to me and probably it isn't until today, how it operated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, your foreign minister and the secretary-general of the foreign ministry took a great interest in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. It was own of our main topics. We were warning for years, especially the secretary-general, of a potential escalation of this region. And Austria took a very great interest in the region and also supporting the Kosovar Albanians. For example, Austria was the only country which recognised the parallel university of Pristina and accepting their diplomas so they could continue studying in Austria.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a problem, wasn't it, that in other countries the diplomas obtained from Pristina University were often not accepted.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the rule. The exception was some private universities or maybe Turkey or some Turkish universities. But Austria was the only one as such accepting diplomas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the concern and foresight that the Austrian government had regarding Kosovo no doubt kicked up a gear once you took over the presidency of the EU.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, in your capacity as part of the foreign ministry with concern for Kosovo, no doubt you tried to read whatever information that was available concerning Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No doubt, those included open sources like newspapers.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also. And then we had our observers on the ground, our monitors, starting in May of 1998. And then the observing and monitoring missions would be growing in the course of the year, of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course those observer missions, no doubt, would send you confidential briefings.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had daily reports and they had weekly and monthly -- yes, there were many, many, many reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no doubt they were supplemented by your own intelligence reports of the Austrian government?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no intelligence reports that I would be seeing from the Austrian sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of the reports by the mon stores on the ground, they weren't all public, were they?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were restricted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And despite all the resources that were at your disposal, as it were, despite your struggle to find out who was the leadership of the KLA, you couldn't find out at the beginning who were in the leadership.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The monitoring missions, they had a very different mandate. They were not there to find out or to find the high-ranking interlocutors. They were, if you like, monitoring the situation: whether there's a security issue, whether there is destruction, where there were IDPs, but it was not in their mandate to identify the high-ranking structure of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, of course, it was one of your tasks to try and find a valid interlocutor.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went on various missions and you were accompanied by such people as Mr. Slinn, you were jointly trying to find who was in the leadership.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily the leadership, but somebody who was a political representative and could speak in the name of the KLA so that we had somebody to talk to and include them in the broader Kosovo/Albanian spectrum to be able to form a platform for negotiations with Belgrade, to solve the situation, the problem, politically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, you are aware that other governments were also similarly trying to find out who was in the leadership of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. As we've seen in these reports which were made available in May 1999 to the Tribunal, I was citing the US also in search of somebody to talk to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You did cite the United States's position, and you say that Ambassador Holbrooke didn't know whether or not the UCK had an internal chain of command. You reported that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did report that. That's a -- that's sort after a mirror what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you of course reported his comments, that he doubted that there was an internal chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I wrote. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition to exhibit P64 that I've just referred to, you also referred in your memo of the 27th of June, Exhibit 61, that "the UCK command structure remains something of a mystery according to the United States."

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talk about the United States's view that as far as there is a General Staff, it's more a matter of diffuse horizontal command and coordination structures.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wrote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course you go on to highlight the same problem we have been talking about, that the United States's view was that that lack of chain of command could be problematic in terms of involving the UCK in political dialogue.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That horizontal command and coordination structures could pose a problem, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your visits with the KLA, no doubt you struggled repeatedly to try and get the KLA to give you somebody that would be their spokesman.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At a certain moment I thought I had identified somebody, but then because of the retreat from Malisevo, I was not able to contact this person anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that it's possible that the difficulty in finding out who was in the leadership of the KLA was because there was not a clear command structure in the KLA at the time you were making these inquiries?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It could be speculation, yeah. I don't know. I don't know of any clear command structure when I was talking to the people. The nearest indication I had were these numbers assigned to certain persons I was talking to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talk about Mr. Thaqi having the number 3.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talk about Mr. Kadri Veseli having the number 7?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you gave evidence that you thought Mr. Krasniqi had the number 11?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard a number being assigned in relation to Mr. Limaj, did you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you thought that the numbers designated, perhaps, people in the hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I assumed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps in the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: May well be, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that when you went to Malisevo for the first time, you met with Mr. Gani Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you referred to him as Commander Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We -- I don't know whether I have written that, but our understanding was that he was the civilian representative. And I don't know where we got that from, most probably from an ECMM report. Because ECMM had been in Malisevo before. So for us he was the -- sort of the mayor of Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he was also appearing in that talk in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bear with me a moment. If you look at Prosecution Exhibit 56, that's your memoranda to the foreign ministry dated the 24th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I may refer to the English. Can you see the portion in italics which deals with remarks?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, you say in your remarks that Mr. Gani Krasniqi was a commander and took part in the setting up of the KLA in Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But at the time when we met him, he was the mayor and in a civilian position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And when you met Mr. Limaj on the 30th of July, he was introduced as Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was never introduced to you as a regional commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talk about spin. It's right, isn't it, that all sides were concerned to put forward the face that was the most favourable to the international community?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you agree that the KLA of course was concerned about complying with all the necessary protocols, so it would seem that they were organised and they could be given a voice in international diplomacy.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, we just wanted to have an interlocutor. And if they -- the way they presented it was not our issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember that when you saw Mr. Thaqi, Number 3, they were concerned -- he was concerned about protocol. He was apologetic that he was meeting a senior official and said that he excused their conduct because they were soldiers and they were not familiar with the niceties of protocol --

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have been a little unclear in the report, but that was Number 7 who apologised for the previous meeting with the secretary-general where he was a little unprepared. And he then said, well, he sort of knew who he was. But at the end of the day, I think he had no clue who he was talking to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a few days later when you did them the great courtesy of going to Klecka, no doubt they were trying to make a good impression with you. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to comment on that. I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw a photograph a little bit earlier with Mr. Krasniqi sitting on a chair by a table. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you identified, looking at the photograph, that Mr. Limaj was to the right and somebody else was to the left.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't identify that person on the left. Could you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that you have met most of the important people in the KLA, as far as you are aware or you know of them?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I was meeting them three times before -- in June, July, so there cannot be -- I cannot met them all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went to Malisevo for the first time, you saw -- you went past the Komorane checkpoint. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We passed the Komorane checkpoint very often. Sometimes we tried to avoid it, but sometimes we tried to go through. Sometimes the Serb police led us through, and on many occasions they sent us back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a Serb checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a Serb checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a Serb checkpoint, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went to Malisevo for the first time, did you see any KLA checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at the outskirts of Suhareke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you described that in Malisevo you thought that perhaps there was a central command there.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what we had hoped to find there, to find the main interlocutors there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe Malisevo at the time you went there.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a bustling town. It's in a crossroads, north/south and east/west connections. On the roadside there were many stands, people selling cigarettes, whatever. It was very lively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any refugees in Malisevo at that time?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, no. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before you went to Malisevo, if I remember rightly you had heard the name Mr. Gani Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you went to Klecka, had you heard the name Celiku or Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the KLA had to pull out of Malisevo in face of the Serb summer offensive. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. After the fighting in Rahovec/Orahovac, the Serbs thought that they had the perfect chance to launch an offensive, because the way they portrayed it, that Rahovec/Orahovac was attacked by the KLA, they had the right to retaliate. And under this pressure, as far as we understood, the KLA retreated from Malisevo into the mountains.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have described the journey from Pristina via Lipljan towards Stimlje en route to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any KLA checkpoint on that road before you got to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was very far already up in the hills there was -- we were stopped -- it wasn't a checkpoint as such, but there was a soldier stopping us. We had to wait there so that the arrangements could be made before we continued to the building where we had the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was right on the very outskirts of Klecka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on this ridge, yes. It was, I don't know, a few hundred metres or something away from the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as far as the journey goes by road in the British armoured Land Rover from Pristina to Stimlje and via the national park in Lipovica, did you see any KLA checkpoints on that entire journey?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first one you saw was the one you described in the hills of Klecka.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not a checkpoint as such, but we were stopped there to -- that they check who we were and that they can prepare the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, after the KLA had to leave Malisevo, are you aware that the Serb press was full of suggestions that the KLA had been defeated?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the KLA had to leave Malisevo, did you read in the Serb press that the KLA had in fact been defeated?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. But I don't think it would have been fair, anyways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember speaking to Mr. Limaj in Klecka on 30 July 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that I spoke to him. I spoke to Jakup Krasniqi, and I don't know whether he talked or not. I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try and refresh your memory, and please tell me if it's -- if I'm correct or not. Do you remember Mr. Limaj speaking to you through the interpreter Baton Haxhiu that the talk of government was not important to him, that what was important was the international community persuading the Serbs to create a corridor so that the civilians could leave the conflict area to go to a safe area?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall apart from what I wrote written in my notes, and they are the only ones refreshing my mind, that they wanted the return of the IDPs because there were some around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, if you could bear with us a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, could you have a look at Prosecution Exhibit 58, that's your handwritten notes following the meeting in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bear with me a moment. Now, you talk about the concern of the KLA members, Mr. Thaqi and Mr. Krasniqi, to arrange in effect a cease-fire before negotiations could proceed. Is that fair or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Thaqi was not at that meeting --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krasniqi. The idea was, just to give you the context again, we were talking about a united platform of the Kosovar Albanian actors, and we thought this could only be done if the KLA would refrain as much as the Serbian side from offensive actions, from attacks. And I wouldn't call it cease-fire, but as I've written in my three conditions for not attacking, not conducting offensive actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you make in your notes the comment that "if Serbs do not accept, there's no longer a front war (people removed)." Do you remember making that comment?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's written in my notes. It's not 100 per cent clear to me what I meant -- what I -- what was the meaning of it. But in my report, I have stated then that they said that they would change their tactics from clear lines -- I mean they had Malisevo, and it was a clear line which area they controlled, to guerrilla actions afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you can think back to that day some years ago right now, in fact what was being said was that if the KLA could no longer conduct an offensive with a front line there was a danger -- there was a difficulty for the KLA in that all these civilians had been displaced and these civilians needed to be looked after.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The IDPs were there already. When they retreated from Malisevo, Malisevo was empty. There was nobody there. The same bustling down which I was describing to you before was almost empty. There was nobody there except the Serbian security forces and a few leftover civilians, but nothing compared to what I had seen before. So these people had to be somewhere. They were IDPs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those IDPs, they were looked after by the KLA in large measure. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say, but they were in areas where the KLA was present as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't remember Mr. Limaj saying that his concern was for the civilians and his primary concern was humanitarian to make sure there was a corridor so they could go from places of conflict to places of safety, or of relative safety?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I can't recall. But the issue of safe return as such was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, the weakness or relative weakness of the KLA is made clear in your briefing of the 31st of July, that's Prosecution Exhibit 59, when you say that the KLA confirmed that they were going to change their tactics.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether that's a weakness or not, but it's just an answer to a changing situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that if they didn't have the capacity to fight a war with clear front lines, they would resort to guerrilla actions?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's everywhere in the world. If you have a superior opponent in weaponry, you have to change your tactics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they did face an overwhelming superior force, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb police forces had APCs, for example, and I don't -- yeah, that's certainly something that the KLA didn't have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard an awful lot of Serb propaganda during your time in Kosovo, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of -- I mean, especially on Kosovo. They published white books they -- of what they called terrorist attacks and how many people were missing or were killed. That was the regular and updated thing they distributed to the embassies in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these white books taken seriously by the embassies or were they viewed with a great deal of circumspection?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wanted to rely on our monitors and observers on the ground, but they, of course, didn't have an overview because there were at the beginning very view and later on you just don't get the full picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, generally speaking of course, you were in possession of the white books and you heard what the monitors said. But is it right that these white books were viewed with a great deal of circumspection by the international community, as being in many places, nothing but Serb propaganda?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We regarded them as being exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a kind word, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm a diplomat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm afraid I'm a lawyer. You wouldn't disagree with me if I said it was propaganda?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't give them much credibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because, of course, you talk about the reluctance of the Austrian ministry to be drawn into propaganda games.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave an example that you declined to take part in a visit arranged by the Serb authorities to Prekaz.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because your view was there was a very great danger that you would be used as a pawn in a propaganda campaign that was conducted by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact you give another example that when in fact in early May or in late May/early June 1998 when you went to Decani, that this was also a propaganda stunt by the FRY.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We feared that, but in a way it was also a known goal by their side because they had shown that they were not in control of what they had tried to portray that they were in control of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So an attempt at propaganda, but not very wise propaganda.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had so much conflicting information that we took the risk to participate at a low level -- meaning my level -- in this visit, where some countries participate on an ambassadorial visit. Most of the EU countries just sent second secretaries or first secretaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's very helpful. Could you look at Prosecution Exhibit 60. That's your report to the foreign ministry, dated the 8 June 1998. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking for it. I've got it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the second page, in which you detail the briefing given to you by the Yugoslav foreign minister and the Ministry of the Interior. That's the five bullet points at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You report, don't you, that the foreign ministry and the Ministry of the Interior of the FRY in effect were denying very largely the international refugee problem?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So much so that the Serb propaganda, I say, extended to the fact that they said that these refugees were all dressed to look the part.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- yeah, well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's fair to say, isn't it, that whenever the Serbs had a chance to make allegations against the KLA or to minimise their role in the crisis, the Serbian role in the crisis, they did so?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is part of what I said, the spin, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, apart from your dealings with the KLA, you dealt with the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both in Pristina and in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You dealt with them right from your arrival in Belgrade in 1997 until perhaps your departure.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to varying degrees. I had little contacts in the foreign ministry itself, because you would not have any frank talks there. But it was, if I say, tradition that going down to Pristina and seeing Kosovo bringing in party leaders, you would also see the prefect of Kosovo, the Serb prefect, Mirko Dautovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a man who gave an awful lot of weight to what he said, the prefect of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sounds very little, but I think he had quite a position in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He knew what the Belgrade line was, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all your time dealing with the Serbs during this period, you never heard any allegations about a prison camp in Lapusnik, did you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard before or after your July meeting with Mr. Limaj in 1998 allegations that there had been a massacre in the mountains in Berisa conducted by the KLA, did you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your experience and your knowledge of the Serbs and the spin that was used, are you of the opinion that if they had such information they would not hesitate to have used it?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they have used other information, whether false or correct. They have alleged that there were I don't know how many people, but killed in Klecka, for example. Then they brought up the issue of Glodjena [inaudible]. So there were some issues they were mentioning to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And going back to Klecka, what was the allegation that the Serbs made regarding Klecka?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They found in a pit or something, they found --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had it been a lime pit?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be. They found human remains.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they say about that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they were killed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And did anything take place after that allegation was made by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what was taken place by the Serbs or what they did --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did, for example, the a Finnish forensic team get involved?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. That was one of the outcomes of the October negotiations which established the OCKVM. There was also pressure to have independent forensic experts study the alleged killing sites. And the Austrian EU Presidency was involved in that. And we had picked six sites for them to study.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact no doubt you are aware of Serb press reports saying that up to 200 people were killed in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I can't recall, but this lime pit thing I recall, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not those allegations were found to be founded or nothing more than Serb propaganda?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the final outcome of the investigations by the Finnish forensic experts were. For none of the sites I have seen a final report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as far as your final understanding is concerned you're of the view that that was Serb spin, in order to look as though they're somehow the victims in all of this?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning I didn't very much credibility to the Klecka thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The main point, of course, that I put to you, Mr. Kickert, is that despite this climate of spin, even spin based on total falsehoods, you didn't hear anything about an illegal camp in Lapusnik during your time in Kosovo in 1998, did you?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically. Just general allegations of kidnappings and illegal detention camps. But I'm not aware that they said something about Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't hear anything about Commander Celiku being anything other than a local commander in 1998? You made your own assumptions perhaps, but you never heard it?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just -- he was just introduced as commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course you state that towards the end of 1998 you met Mr. Limaj, together with Mr. Thaqi in Baja.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. A meeting with Ambassador Petritsch where I was there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that around November 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could well be. It was winter, that's for sure, and foggy and I think we were late. And we already drove back when we were called on our cellphones to return so that the meeting could take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if again you could cast your mind back to that foggy day in November 1998, do you remember that on that occasion Mr. Limaj was introduced as a commander of the 121st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't recall whether he was introduced at all. I mean, by that time I knew his face, so I don't know whether he introduced himself or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mention another occasion when on your weekend off, or your weekend anyway, you went to Mr. Limaj's home.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that a lot of people were present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was -- yeah, some people, some men. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you inferred from that that people showed a great deal of respect to Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was -- I think my assessment that he was very well-respected, but this wasn't a surprise to me because he was a commander of the UCK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion you were with a newspaper reporter, is that right, or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a newspaper reporter and a US diplomat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reporter was who?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dugadjin Gorani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if Mr. Gorani had suggested that you go to Mr. Limaj's home because his uncle had just passed away?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I can't recall. It could well be. But it is the case that since we were in the area that Mr. Gorani suggested that we go visit Mr. Limaj. It would make a lot of sense if that was because his uncle passed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of a Kosovan tradition that when a someone passes away the close surviving relatives stay in the house to receive the condolences of people who are close to the family? Have you heard that before?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would bear with me a moment, Mr. Kickert. You give an example of Lum Haxhiu standing next to Mr. Holbrooke and posing for a photograph. Do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was even on the TV screens. That's how -- why I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that Lum Haxhiu didn't break away from the KLA [sic], but that conduct was not welcome?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I understood afterwards, he was just a regular soldier and certainly not somebody who was in a position to speak on behalf of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's the case, isn't it, that in fact from your understanding of what happened that he just of his own volition decided as a person in KLA uniform he would go into the picture. It may look good for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well -- because, I mean, to be photographed with Richard Holbrooke is something like an official recognition. He may have thought that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps you may think that in the absence of clear commands from a centre, people did what they thought was best to help the KLA cause.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be also that he wanted to have a picture taken. I don't know. I was not there. I can't -- everything else would be pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. But you also give an example of some Scandinavians or a -- some UCK members in Scandinavia having discussions with Mr. Holbrooke.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the same person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the same person?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the same person, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said those people, that particular family, had no particular rank or positions. That's in your memo.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is referring to Mr. Lum Haxhiu who was photographed or filmed with Mr. Holbrooke. This refers to this very same person. I think what you're referring to now is what I cite somebody, maybe Demaqi or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is. I'm grateful for that. After the war, you had occasion to speak to Mr. Limaj on several occasions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember in fact his role during the Rambouillet negotiations?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't have the status of a member of delegation, but if I'm not mistaken he was there and entered Rambouillet on these exchange passes to -- as a -- an advisor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware at that time -- you were involved in Rambouillet?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Rambouillet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I might say so in quite an important role as far as the Austrian diplomatic service is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't there in my capacity as an Austrian, but as assistant to Petritsch, the special envoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Limaj was an advocate to the Rambouillet signing up to the agreement. Are you aware of that or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the war in 1999, are you aware of Mr. Limaj's role during the various -- I think in fact it was the administrative agreement, but let me check. How would you describe Mr. Limaj's role in 1999?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a high-ranking PDK official.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever -- was he generally in favour of democracy or was he rather militant?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was absolutely in favour of democracy and reconciliation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he spoke to you in formal settings, did he? In formal meetings and informal meetings, both.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both. We had no problems. In fact informally, when I went to the headquarters of the party and we met and we, as I said before, he had no problem speaking Serbo-Croatian to me, which was our only language of communication, because normally I spoke German or French or English with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear him espouse anything even approaching incitement or violence or any racist attitude towards any ethnic group at all?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in fact keen on establishing an inclusive and democratic Kosovo, with rights for all?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is fair to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact including rights for Serbs, Roma, Bosniaks, and members of other Kosovar Albanian political parties?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, many -- or perhaps many Kosovo politicians would not like to speak Serbo-Croat with you. Would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fair assessment, especially 1999. I want to remind you a UN employee, a Bulgarian, was killed in 1999 because most probably his Bulgarian was mistaken for Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's common knowledge the Serbs had banned the teaching of Albanian in all institutions and government structures in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a parallel system where they did schooling in their university.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you viewed Mr. Limaj's willingness to speak in Serbian as yet another example of him being a decent democrat.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give any other examples of your involvement with Mr. Limaj which would help show the Court what kind of man you think he is?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was a good example of somebody who turned from a soldier to a politician. And there are many of these examples in the KLA, and I dealt with them from 1999 onwards until the present day. And he was running, as far as I'm not mistaken, for mayor of Pristina. And he was regarded highly by the internationals, as a person you could work with very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for that. I'm very grateful for your assistance. If you could wait there, Mr. Kickert, my friend, Mr. Powles, may have some questions for you. But thank you for bearing with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you're going to have to wait until the break unless it's going to be a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: It will be slightly longer than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We have to break because of the tapes. We'll resume at 10 to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Guy-Smith, you don't feel overlooked at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't feel overlooked, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Powles:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, I appear with Mr. Michael Topolski on behalf of Mr. Isak Musliu who sits directly behind me. As I indicated, my cross-examination will be relatively brief and uncontroversial. You first went into Kosovo in the first half of 1998.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went into Kosovo in 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And initially you were went to Pristina with a view to get to know people in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Political representatives, but I also had dealings with the university because of what I mentioned before -- we recognised their diplomas, so I had to make sure that the diplomas presented by Kosovar Albanian students were real ones. And I was dealing also with student leaders. But it was -- all of them were in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, yes. And it was in June of 1998 that a decision was taken to start discussions with the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was in June or in July, but at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And initially it was difficult to do that because, as you said, the structure of the Kosovo Liberation Army was not clear.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no clear spokesperson or contact point within the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the naming of Jakup Krasniqi, there was nobody -- or there was somebody in Geneva --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but -- who we didn't deal with. I was looking for somebody on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: But until Jakup Krasniqi was named, there was no spokesperson as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Kosovo report, the report of the Independent Commission on Kosovo, which was I believe chaired by Justice Richard Goldstone

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may read you a short part of that to get your views upon it to see if it was an accurate description of how things were at that time. It's described in this way: "In July, the US Kosovo Diplomatic Observer Mission, KDOM, was established and it's said in the report that KDOM attempted to unite the disparate fragments of the KLA. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was KDOM as such. I mean, KDOM has various arms. It has a U.S. arm, a Russian arm and an EU arm, the ECMM. But KDOM was involved in these talks, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In trying to unite the disparate parts of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they were doing that, but our aim was to get the disparate political fragments of the Kosovar Albanian society together -- I mean the KLA and the political representatives in Pristina, who were not together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's said in the Kosovo report that KDOM -- officially, in effect, the KDOM office filled a vacuum, as one journalist put it according to the report, finding there was a place where the KLA leadership could be contacted. Is that something you would agree with, that going through KDOM was a possibility of getting to the leadership of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a route the U.S. representatives were going. They used KDOM in the field to get in contact with KLA representatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't know whether they -- which persons they had met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. You had three meetings, if I'm not mistaken, with the KLA in July of 1998.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 22nd, the 23rd, and the 30th of July.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I could re-establish through the reports, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And the meetings on the 22nd of July, the one where you met with Mr. Gani Krasniqi and Mr. Veseli and you went with a journalist, Mr. Baton Haxhiu. And the meeting with organised by Mr. Nick Turnbull, the ECMM monitor.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is correct but Mr. Haxhiu, the journalist, was not going us, not travelling with us. He appeared there, to our surprise, but he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And the second meeting on the 23rd of July, effectively the day after, that was a meeting with Mr. Thaqi and Mr. Veseli. That was a meeting that was -- were you introduced or taken to that meeting by a journalist, Mr. Dugadjin Gorani? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the third meeting on the 30th of July with Mr. David Slinn, again the one where you met with Mr. Krasniqi, Mr. Limaj and Mr. Buja, that was a another meeting arranged by a journalist, Mr. Baton Hazhiu?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, an at the same time, same thing we were there, there was also a BBC TV crew there. So journalists were very good contacts to ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krasniqi became the spokesperson for the Kosovo Liberation Army on the 11th of June.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know when, but in the course of July it was clear that he was a spokesperson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. It became clear to you --

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in early July that he was the spokesperson.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the time we were not sure at the beginning whether he was speaking authoritarily in the name of the KLA or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard I believe, certainly by the 7th of July, that he was a spokesperson for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: By that time I heard more and more people saying, well, this is really somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But you didn't get to meet him, it's fair to say, until the 30th of July.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that meeting arranged through a journalist.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's fair to say, isn't it, that the situation on the ground in Kosovo at that time, in terms of being able to make contact with those that you may want to have made contact with, it wasn't an easy process?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't easy at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A fairly chaotic situation.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially after the Serb offensive started and militia was vacated. Then sort of I lost the point where I could meet them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But also fairly difficult to identify within the organisation who were the right person to speak to and thereafter to make a meeting point to go and meet them.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I had thought that meeting Number 3 was quite a good contact, but afterwards it was not possible to meet him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. On the KLA side it's fair to say that there was some confusion as to who the official spokesperson was. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you would have to ask the KLA whether they had a confusion or not. I can just tell what my perception was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take you through a few incidents. On the 24th of June I think it was, that was the date that Mr. Lum Haxhiu met or was able to push himself into the photograph with Mr. Holbrooke in Munich.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but if you say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that's the right date; I may be mistaken myself. That incident was referred to by Mr. Krasniqi at an interview that he gave to Der Spiegel. That interview in the newspaper is contained -- have you received a bundle of documents entitled "Documents which may be used in cross-examination of Mr. Kickert"? I don't know if that's in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't received that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Allow me -- I'll make arrangements. Have Your Honours received it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Have the Prosecution received it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I gather we are about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm afraid it's not tabulated. Defence, as Your Honours know, don't have the advantage of having the technology facilities that the Prosecution have got and on this occasion we don't even have a binder and tabs to assist. But if you allow me to draw your attention, I think it's to the fifth document in the bundle, an entitled UCK spokesman's goal of unification of Albanians. The U number is U008-3955. It's the fifth statement-document behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found that, Mr. Kickert?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Have Your Honours managed to locate the article?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the second page of the article about halfway down there's a question: "Der Spiegel: Reportedly, the UCK is fragmented into several groups that are quarreling about direction. Is there a central command? Do the orders come from here or abroad? Mr. Krasniqi's response is: "The UCK has only one main staff and one supreme commander. The military decisions are made here in Kosovo. At the moment, I am the only one permitted to speak on behalf of the UCK." He then goes on, Mr. Krasniqi -- a question is put about Robert Gelbard: "The U.S. special envoy to the Balkans, recently talked to one of your activists in Switzerland. And Mr. Krasniqi's response is: "This was an attempt by Rugova to present to the Americans a UCK activist loyal to the LDK."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down in reading the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "We have our people in Switzerland, but Gelbard's interlocutor was not an authorised representative of our movement." The next question, I believe, is a question relating to the meeting with Mr. Holbrooke of Lum Haxhiu. The question is: "U.S. mediator Richard Holbrooke is obviously in favour of including the UCK in search for a settlement to the conflict. He met with UCK representatives in Kosovo. Do you feel validated by that?" And his response is: "No, Holbrooke did not speak with the proper representatives and this was not his first mistaken evaluation of the situation." So Mr. Krasniqi there seeming to imply that Lum Haxhiu in his meeting with Mr. Holbrooke was not an authorised representative of the KLA. If you would turn to the first document in the bundle, it's the ICG report, "Kosovo's Long Hot Summer," and turn to page 4. There's a -- the third paragraph, the last sentence of that paragraph. There's a quotation of Mr. Krasniqi's from an interview that he gave to a Kosovo newspaper, Koha Ditore, and he says about this about his interview that he gave to Der Spiegel: "There was a mistake in the interview I gave to Der Spiegel. They are legitimate representatives of the UCK who have the authority to talk in the name of the UCK with various representatives and diplomats abroad." So would you agree, Mr. Kickert, that it seems that even Mr. Krasniqi doesn't seem entirely clear as to who was authorised to speak on behalf of the KLA at that time?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say what he meant, Mr. Krasniqi. But to my knowledge the -- Mr. Gelbard met with Balrin Mahmuti [phoen] in Geneva and, as far as I understood, he was speaking on behalf of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But in his initial interview in Der Spiegel, Mr. Krasniqi indicated that they weren't official spokespersons for the KLA and it's later he is himself corrected as to who was and who was not authorised to speak on the part of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would probably have to ask Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to something you wrote then. You refer to Mr. Lum Haxhiu in I think it's Prosecution Exhibit 56, your memo of the 24th of July. If you could turn to the last -- I think it's the last sentence of your report. You refer to Mr. Lum Haxhiu, the simple soldier who placed himself at the right-hand side of the photo during Holbrooke's visit to Munich. And you say "according to the headquarters in Malisevo," that's obviously the KLA headquarters, he's "instructed not to make any further comments, which he is now respecting." So you were told, and you'll correct me if I'm wrong, you were told that an instruction had been given to Mr. Haxhiu not to given any further comments.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The "simple soldier" is under quotation because this is probably what I was told when I was in Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there's a little translation error as well. It's not on the right-hand side but it says "brought himself into the right picture." So he wanted to be in the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this, they have told him that he should not talk to the press anymore, because after that visit he was looked for by the press because they thought, meeting Holbrooke, he must be some important person. So the press went after him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If you could turn to I believe it's the fourth or the -- sorry, the sixth document in the bundle that's been handed up. And I think it's a document entitled "UCK predicts Successful March on Pristina." Have you found that document, Mr. Kickert?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's an article that appeared in Koha Ditore on the same date I think that you wrote your report, the 24th of July 1998. And it's an "'exclusive' interview with Lum Haxhiu, Kosovo Liberation Army officer for Combat Morale, National Policy, and Information in the region of Reka [sic]." So it would appear that the message had not quite got through to Mr. Haxhiu. If again you could turn to the first document, the ICG report, "Kosovo's Long Hot Summer." If I may draw your attention to one part of it which was the International Crisis Group's evaluation of Mr. Krasniqi's abilities as the public relations officer of the KLA. It starts at the bottom of page 4 of that document and goes on to page 5. What I will do is if I can read you the evaluation of the International Crisis Group, and if you could afterwards say if it's something that you agree with it or not. They say that: "In many ways Krasniqi simply epitomises the understandably unsophisticated public relations of the UCK. While the inconsistencies of his declarations could be dismissed as trivial, they, nevertheless, illustrate the difficult task that the international mediators have faced finding interlocutors in Kosovo." Would you agree that as an international mediator you had difficulties in identifying appropriate interlocutors in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they go on: "Similar liberation movements in other countries are usually led either by a personality who came back from abroad or else by some local leader gone underground and resurfaced in a guerrilla uniform." And they go on: "With the UCK no such leader has emerged and on what seemed to be a weekly basis, journalists interviewed UCK representatives, each apparently claiming to be the rebels' "commandant", each with a different story."
