Would you agree with that evaluation that's given by the International Crisis Group?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We certainly had no clear picture of the leadership of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to spin and, again, more evaluation of Mr. Krasniqi. I think it's the fifth document that's been handed up. It's a -- an article -- I'm so sorry. I think it's the fourth document. The fourth document handed out. It's entitled beater seeks --

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: I am reminded to slow down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a document entitled "BETA Sees UCK 'Seriously Shaken.'" A four-page document. If I could turn your attention to page 3 of that article, third paragraph down. Some evaluation of Mr. Krasniqi: "After Orahovac, many Albanian intellectuals started to criticise in lowered voices 'adventurism' and 'irresponsibility' of the KLA commanders and denied 'intellectual capacities' of some of the leading 'people in the woods.' Spokesman Krasniqi was the main target of their criticism, because he could not cope with his duties." And the article goes on: "To illustrate his 'stupidity and illiteracy,' they often mentioned the fact that the KLA handed over 35 Serbian civilians to the International Red Cross, while it occurred to no one to invite a foreign TV crew to report on the event, thus scoring new points for the KLA." So it would appear from that article that in terms of the spin that the KLA were able to present in no way at all matched the capabilities of the Serbian spin doctors, if you could call them that. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't comment on that. I just know that the statement of Mr. Krasniqi, talk about a unified homeland for the Albanians didn't serve them well, and he retracted from that. This is something which didn't go well with the international community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was I think one of the inconsistencies of Mr. Krasniqi that was referred to in the International Crisis Group report, where they drew or made some criticisms of Mr. Krasniqi in terms of his being the spokesperson for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Many times even spokespersons of international organisations have to retract what they have said before. So, yeah. But it's your call, what you want to qualify it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In -- it was from November of 1997 that you were based in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Austrian embassy in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, no doubt, received reports in your capacity -- in the embassy in Belgrade, reports on what was going on in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was mainly media reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in those media reports, and indeed any other information that you received, were you aware that Serb forces were conducting attacks on the Albanian -- Kosovar Albanian, civilian population in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to a certain incident?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could assist. Were there any incidents that you are aware of civilians being attacked in Kosovo in the early part of 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the Serbian security forces?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to recall. I mean, what then triggered the whole conflict to escalate were the operations the Serbian security forces conducted in Drenica in the very end of February and the beginning of March of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there civilian casualties as a result of those activities?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were indeed, among the Jashari family. There were children and women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it was 18 women and 10 children.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could well be. But there was a large number of women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was one amongst a number of districts where there was civilian casualties on the Kosovar Albanian side at the hands of the Serbian authorities in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the civilians were those who suffered the most in the whole conflict, in general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed there were some -- as I think you've referred to already -- some concerns by the Austrian government as to what was being done at the hands of the Serbs in Kosovo at that time. Indeed, you were invited by the Serb authorities to go to Prekaz in March 1998, and that was something that was turned down by your government.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We considered that as a propaganda stunt. But at the same time, two colleagues of mine, a Brit and a Swede, went on their own to Prekaz to see what had happened, and from them I got first-hand report how it looked like. And afterwards the military attaches of various embassies were also in the area and also at the morgue in Skenderaj, looking at the victims of these assaults.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If I could turn your attention to the last document in the bundle. In the right-hand corner you'll see the numbers or the letter R and on 025-781. Have you got that document, Mr. Kickert?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a report it seems from "EU KDG CC Pristina/Medical Adviser, OPS, PIO." Do you know who the author of this report might be? Not the person, but the authority.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was certainly ECMM. It looks like an ECMM report. "Medical adviser," there was at that time an Austrian doctor in the ECMM team in Pristina. So he could be the author.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says: "To: RC Belgrade HC ECMM Sarajevo." And then the last thing: "Austrian Embassy." Would that be your embassy, the Austrian Embassy?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be our embassy, because we had the EU presidency at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we would presume this was perhaps a document that would have passed before you in your capacity in the Austrian Embassy at the time?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we may go through some of the things contained in the report. "Headlines." It says: "Thousands of Displaced People surviving in poor conditions. "Signs of spreading communicable diseases. "Urgent need of drinking water and nutrition. Then it says, "Destruction and vandalism in the Malisevo area increasing daily. "Serb police forces looting shops in Malisevo, and torching premises. "Graves in Orahovac." And I should say the date of this report is the 6th of August, 1998. The summary indicates that it's a report relating to period of July the 28th and August the 5th and the authors of the report are then referred to. Under July the 29th on the second page of the document it says that: "Police was present along the road and seem to be in control of the area between Komorane and Orahovac. Only one old man was seen in Malisevo as he was escorted by some policemen into a building when patrol entered the village." Can you see that under, July 29th?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, more importantly, at the bottom of the page under August 2nd: "Joint (EU&US&RussFed) patrol visited the Malisevo-Banja-Suva Reka [sic] area." And then, crucially, they say driving through Lapusnik 5 km west of Komorane patrol saw some burning houses but nobody being around." The report goes on: "The number of dead animals around Malisevo was larger than two days before. Patrol went to Banja 4 km south-east of Malisevo and saw mortar attacks on the street and a destroyed mosque tower in Banja. Approached by local civilians in Banja patrol learned that almost all inhabitants of Malisevo and Banja left their homes before the Security Forces offensive some days before." And then it goes on: "They are still afraid of massacres and hide in nearby hills. Patrol went up to Krvasorija 6 km southeast of Malisevo to visit DPs there." Then they say, "Some 600 individuals were hiding in the bushes and woods. Patrol saw them living without shelter in poor hygienic conditions which facilitate the spreading of communicable diseases. Medical Adviser saw some sick individuals, suffering from febrile diarrhoea and respiratory infections." And then it goes on to the third page. And then it says: "On the way back through Lapusnik, a deserted village we saw some more burning premises than some hours before," indicating perhaps there were properties being burned in Lapusnik at that time. And then under August the 4th, the last two sentences -- sorry, the beginning of August the 4th. "Combined (EU&US) patrol went to Malisevo and observed policemen looting shops there." And then at the bottom of that paragraph under August the 4th: "On the way back to Komorane policemen in Lapusnik were observed setting fire in a farmhouse. Some dozens of premises were destroyed, some still burning at that time." And the reference to the forces and police forces, they would be Serb forces in that report?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they would. And as I indicated before, when I travelled to Malisevo after it was abandoned by the KLA, you would see -- every time you would go through Malisevo you would see more destruction. So every time there was -- even once we were there they used a bulldozer to take down buildings in Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the ECMM observers also saw somebody - I don't know whether that's the same incident - a uniformed Serb policeman with a can of petroleum setting fire to a house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But from this report you would agree that from July 28th onwards there's a report of Serb forces destroying property in Lapusnik and indeed elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a pattern which we saw that in villages, houses where there was no inhabitants, we would pass by and then these houses were torched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It even happened to the EU political director's troika when we went at the end of July, that on the way we saw fields which were okay; on the way back they were burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Serb forces responsible for that?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We assume, because there was no civilians around and just the Serb police forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this report also referring to Serb --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly make pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this report refer to Serb policemen conducting looting?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They saw themselves the monitors and reported on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, but they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the consequences, it would seem, for the civilian population in this area were quite devastating and that they were forced to flee.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the reason why we in August of 1998, we saw a humanitarian crisis looming, not only because of this report - we were aware of that. And this is why at that time the commissioner who was responsible for humanitarian affairs was visiting. And we tried with the deployment of our monitors to deploy them all other Kosovo so that through their presence there will be some feeling of security so that they would return out of the hills into the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You never actually went to Lapusnik, did you, Mr. Kickert?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you had heard of several fights being conducted there during the war.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see that. If you used the main road, you would see the impacts of bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It may not be something that you can assist with, but did you know where the front line was in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, again, this may be outside your area of interest or expertise, Mr. Kickert, but also it may be something that you're able to assist the Trial Chamber with and it's on that basis it's something that I put to you. In early 1998, Serb forces and in particular the intelligence side of Serb forces, they were relatively sophisticated at that side, certainly compared to the Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not comment on that. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's fair to say that the Serb forces had recent experience or certainly experience conducting warfare in other Yugoslav republics.

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's your interpretation and they certainly had experience, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of Serb forces infiltrating the Kosovo Liberation Army with spies or informants?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of Serb forces using any Albanians as informers during that period?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not something you heard about?

utterances.speaker: JAN KICKERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kickert.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please go a little more slowly than we have recently. The interpreters are in difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I will. Your Honour, I would simply ask that this exhibit with the ERN U008-3969 which was presented to the witness, if that could be given an exhibit number. A Prosecution Exhibit number is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P65.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And the document with ERN --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you just pause one moment while we attempt to find it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Certainly. I apologise. Your Honour, if it's any assistance, if these go into evidence, I don't feel that I need to put questions to the witness on them. So it may not be necessary that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is not a matter of assistance but this has now become a Prosecution exhibit. That's the BETA article.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And the other document bears the ERN U008-3955 on the first page, and the headline is "UCK Spokesman: Goal is Unification of All Albanians."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the Der Spiegel?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's correct. And I would ask for a Prosecution number for that document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P66.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: On that basis, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask your indulgence. I omitted to ask that the last document that was put to the witness, the report dated the 6th of August, could that be made a Defence exhibit, please. I believe that would be DM2, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kickert, as you may have gathered in all that technical procedure just then, there are no further questions for you. May the Chamber thank you very much for your attendance and the assistance you've given, and we wish you well on your journey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question arises, I think -- Mr. Nicholls, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- whether 23 minutes is practical for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm at the Chamber's disposal. We need to prepare the courtroom before the witness could enter. I'm happy to start or we can start tomorrow. We won't get very much done today. I think I will finish tomorrow, in any event, if I start tomorrow. So it's fine with me if we were to break now and send the witness home. He has been here for quite some time. Otherwise it's -- I'm at the Chamber's disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We think it would be an appropriate course to adjourn early this evening and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of November, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
